cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio is dedicated to helping public-sector clients navigate the complexities of policy, management, and regulatory challenges. We don't just provide services; we deliver innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality solutions that drive meaningful change.
We estimate the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. But we don't stop there. We also evaluate program effectiveness, ensuring that solutions don't just look good on paper—they work in the real world.
We collaborate with virtually all federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector clients. Our key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
As an Economics Analyst, you will provide applied research and consulting services in support of national-level programs focused primarily on addressing a variety of policy issues. You will provide a wide range of support services to improve the effectiveness of regulatory and non-regulatory programs and assess their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific Duties May Include
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues, on a variety of topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection. Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs. Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts. Provide general program support, such as data collection, literature review, report writing, and presentation preparation.
You will work in collaboration with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team that includes economists, scientists, and engineers. You will also have direct contact with clients and will contribute to expanding our business.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree plus 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree) in economics, public policy, science, or a related discipline with strong quantitative skills and an outstanding academic record.
1+ Year experience in MS Office applications, particularly Excel.
Demonstrated knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python).
Demonstrated skills (through employment or academic coursework) in the following areas: economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, as this is a client-facing role.
Very strong analytical skills and a demonstrated ability to work independently and to apply a variety of technical skills and innovative thinking to solve problems.
Ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
Preferred Requirements
Prior consulting experience.
Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis.
Knowledge of or exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio.

The team estimates the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. We also evaluate program effectiveness to ensure solutions work in practice, not just on paper.
Our clients include federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector organizations. Key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0160.responsibilities:
In this role, you will carry out applied research and consulting in support of national-level programs focused on a range of policy issues. You will support regulatory and non-regulatory programs by assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific duties may include:
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues across topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection.
Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs.
Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts.
Provide general program support, including data collection, literature review, report writing, and preparation of written materials.
You will coordinate with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team of economists, scientists, and engineers. The role also involves direct contact with clients and contributes to business development.
cond_0160.requirements:
Bachelor's degree plus 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree) in economics, public policy, science, or a related discipline with strong quantitative skills and a solid academic record.
1+ Year experience in MS Office applications, particularly Excel.
Demonstrated knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python).
Demonstrated skills (through employment or academic coursework) in the following areas: economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Prior consulting experience is highly desirable.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting skills are essential, as the role involves client contact.
Strong analytical skills and a demonstrated ability to work independently and apply a range of technical skills and sound judgment to solve problems.
Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines and coordinate effectively within a team.
Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis.
Knowledge of or exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio.
cond_0160.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0304.intro:
We are looking for an Economics Analyst to join our Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio at [Company name masked], which supports public-sector clients on policy, management, and regulatory challenges.
The team estimates the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. We also evaluate program effectiveness to ensure solutions work in practice, not just on paper.
Our clients include federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector organizations. Key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0304.responsibilities:
In this role, you will carry out applied research and consulting in support of national-level programs focused on a range of policy issues. You will support regulatory and non-regulatory programs by assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific duties may include:
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues across topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection.
Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs.
Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts.
Provide general program support, including data collection, literature review, report writing, and preparation of written materials.
You will coordinate with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team of economists, scientists, and engineers. The role also involves direct contact with clients and contributes to business development.
cond_0304.requirements:
Bachelor's degree plus 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree) in economics, public policy, science, or a related discipline with strong quantitative skills and a solid academic record.
1+ Year experience in MS Office applications, particularly Excel.
Demonstrated knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python).
Demonstrated skills (through employment or academic coursework) in the following areas: economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Prior consulting experience is highly desirable.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting skills are essential, as the role involves client contact.
Strong analytical skills and a demonstrated ability to work independently and apply a range of technical skills and sound judgment to solve problems.
Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines and coordinate effectively within a team.
Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis.
Knowledge of or exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio.

[Company name masked]'s Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio is dedicated to helping public-sector clients navigate the complexities of policy, management, and regulatory challenges. We don't just provide services; we deliver innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality solutions that drive meaningful change.
We estimate the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. But we don't stop there. We also evaluate program effectiveness, ensuring that solutions don't just look good on paper—they work in the real world.
We collaborate with virtually all federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector clients. Our key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0325.responsibilities:
As an Economics Analyst, you will provide applied research and consulting services in support of national-level programs focused primarily on addressing a variety of policy issues. You will provide a wide range of support services to improve the effectiveness of regulatory and non-regulatory programs and assess their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific Duties May Include
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues, on a variety of topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection. Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs. Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts. Provide general program support, such as data collection, literature review, report writing, and presentation preparation.
You will work in collaboration with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team that includes economists, scientists, and engineers. You will also have direct contact with clients and will contribute to expanding our business.
cond_0325.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree plus 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree) in economics, public policy, science, or a related discipline with strong quantitative skills and an outstanding academic record.
1+ Year experience in MS Office applications, particularly Excel.
Demonstrated knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python).
Demonstrated skills (through employment or academic coursework) in the following areas: economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, as this is a client-facing role.
Very strong analytical skills and a demonstrated ability to work independently and to apply a variety of technical skills and innovative thinking to solve problems.
Ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
Preferred Requirements
Prior consulting experience.
Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis.
Knowledge of or exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio.
cond_0325.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0372.intro:
We are looking for an Economics Analyst to join our team.
[Company name masked]'s Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio is dedicated to helping public-sector clients navigate the complexities of policy, management, and regulatory challenges. We don't just provide services; we deliver innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality solutions that drive meaningful change.
We estimate the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. But we don't stop there. We also evaluate program effectiveness, ensuring that solutions don't just look good on paper—they work in the real world.
We collaborate with virtually all federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector clients. Our key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0372.responsibilities:
As an Economics Analyst, you will provide applied research and consulting services in support of national-level programs focused primarily on addressing a variety of policy issues. You will provide a wide range of support services to improve the effectiveness of regulatory and non-regulatory programs and assess their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific duties may include:
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues, on a variety of topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection. Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs. Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts. Provide general program support, such as data collection, literature review, report writing, and presentation preparation.
You will work in collaboration with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team that includes economists, scientists, and engineers. You will also have direct contact with clients and will contribute to expanding our business.
cond_0372.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in economics, public policy, science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus around 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree), with solid quantitative skills and a good academic record. Around 1 year of experience with MS Office applications, particularly Excel. Working knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python). Background in the following areas (through employment or academic coursework): economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Prior consulting experience is a plus. As this is a client-facing role, the ability to communicate effectively in writing and verbally is important. Strong analytical skills and a willingness to work independently and apply a range of technical skills to solve problems. Ability to work well in a team and manage multiple tasks and deadlines. Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis. Exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio, is helpful.

cond_0434.responsibilities:

Deep knowledge of economic and policy analysis methods, working with economic data, and model development and application (demonstrated through employment or academic coursework).

cond_0443.responsibilities:

Strong analytical abilities and a demonstrated ability to work independently and to apply a variety of technical skills and innovative thinking to solve problems. [Company name masked]'s Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio is dedicated to helping public-sector clients navigate the complexities of policy, management, and regulatory challenges. We don't just provide services; we deliver innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality solutions that drive meaningful change.
We estimate the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. But we don't stop there. We also evaluate program effectiveness, ensuring that solutions don't just look good on paper—they work in the real world.
We collaborate with virtually all federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector clients. Our key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0452.responsibilities:
As an Economics Analyst, you will provide applied research and consulting services in support of national-level programs focused primarily on addressing a variety of policy issues. You will provide a wide range of support services to improve the effectiveness of regulatory and non-regulatory programs and assess their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific Duties May Include
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues, on a variety of topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection. Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs. Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts. Provide general program support, such as data collection, literature review, report writing, and presentation preparation.
You will work in collaboration with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team that includes economists, scientists, and engineers. You will also have direct contact with clients and will contribute to expanding our business.
cond_0452.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in economics, public policy, science, or a related discipline required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
Minimum 2 years of demonstrated expertise in a relevant field, with a strong quantitative background and an outstanding academic record.
Proven track record of expertise in MS Office applications, particularly Excel.
Advanced knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python).
Deep knowledge of economic and policy analysis methods, working with economic data, and model development and application (demonstrated through employment or academic coursework).
Exceptional written and oral communication skills, as this is a client-facing role.
Strong analytical abilities and demonstrated capacity to work independently, applying a range of technical skills and sound judgment to solve problems.
Preferred Requirements
Prior consulting experience is highly desirable.
Solid understanding of regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis.
Proficiency in data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio.
Strong ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple tasks and deadlines.

[Company name masked]'s Regulatory, Policy, and Economics business portfolio is dedicated to helping public-sector clients navigate the complexities of policy, management, and regulatory challenges. We don't just provide services; we deliver innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality solutions that drive meaningful change.
We estimate the environmental, safety, and social impacts of regulations, policies, and programs, assessing their costs, benefits, and economic impacts. But we don't stop there. We also evaluate program effectiveness, ensuring that solutions don't just look good on paper—they work in the real world.
We collaborate with virtually all federal agencies, state and local agencies, and select non-profit and private-sector clients. Our key clients include the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Agriculture, Department of Transportation, and the Department of Homeland Security.
cond_0480.responsibilities:
As an Economics Analyst, you will provide applied research and consulting services in support of national-level programs focused primarily on addressing a variety of policy issues. You will provide a wide range of support services to improve the effectiveness of regulatory and non-regulatory programs and assess their costs, benefits, and economic impacts.
Specific duties may include:
Conduct research and analysis on policy issues, on a variety of topics such as transportation, security, labor, health, and environmental protection. Perform cost-benefit, economic modeling, statistical/econometric, or other quantitative analyses to assess the impacts of regulations, policies, and programs. Develop analytical methods, databases, and models using Excel, R, or other software to quantify costs, benefits, or other regulatory impacts. Provide general program support, such as data collection, literature review, report writing, and presentation preparation.
You will work in collaboration with senior and junior staff within a multidisciplinary team that includes economists, scientists, and engineers. You will also have direct contact with clients and will contribute to expanding our business.
cond_0480.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in economics, public policy, science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus around 2 years of relevant work experience (or a Master's degree), with solid quantitative skills and a good academic record. Around 1 year of experience with MS Office applications, particularly Excel. Working knowledge of data analysis and modeling approaches and scripting software (e.g., R, Stata, Python). Background in the following areas (through employment or academic coursework): economic and policy analysis methods; working with economic data; model development and application.
Prior consulting experience is a plus. As this is a client-facing role, the ability to communicate effectively in writing and verbally is important. Strong analytical skills and a willingness to work independently and apply a range of technical skills to solve problems. Ability to work well in a team and manage multiple tasks and deadlines. Familiarity with regulatory and policy analysis frameworks and tools, such as cost-benefit analysis and economic impact analysis. Exposure to data visualization and dashboarding software, such as Tableau, Power BI, or Google Data Studio, is helpful.
